sections.title: Overview
sections.content: APEXlang lets teams read and review source-controlled Oracle APEX definitions. Builder synchronization and SQLcl validate the final behavior.

sections.title: Reading APEXlang Syntax
sections.content:
Use a component identifier within its component scope. Local references use @ and Global Page or Universal Theme references use @/. Use fenced code blocks for SQLcl export examples and fenced code block samples.

```sql
select *
from demo_customers;
```

```javascript-browser
apex.message.showPageSuccess("Saved");
```

sections.title: Using Coding Agents
sections.content: Review the component identifier, staticId usage, and Builder synchronization expectations before asking a coding agent to modify APEXlang source.

sections.title: Using SQLcl
sections.content: Use SQLcl export, SQLcl validate, and SQLcl import as the authoritative workflow around APEXlang changes.

sections.title: Builder And External Tools
sections.content: Builder synchronization matters when external tools or coding agents change shared component references, page item definitions, or Universal Theme assets.
